statements: We are adding gradual rollout to the feature flags in this repository over a few messages. Keep everything working as you go. The decisions below hold for all of it.

Decision A: a flag's answer for a user is deterministic. The user's bucket is fnv1a32 of the text flagName:userId, from src/hash.mjs, taken modulo 100. The same flag, user and settings always give the same answer.
Decision B: checking a flag never throws. A flag that was never defined is off, and its name is added to store.unknown the first time it is checked, once only.

Decision C: every change to a flag appends one entry to store.audit, shaped { type, at, name }, where type is the operation's name and at is store.clock(). A refused change appends nothing. Changes return { ok: true, value } or { ok: false, error: { code } }: an undefined flag has code not_found and a bad argument has code invalid.

First, add setRollout(store, name, percent), where percent is a whole number from 0 to 100, and change isEnabled to isEnabled(store, name, userId). An enabled flag is on for a user whose bucket is below its percent. A flag with no rollout set is on for everyone when it is enabled, as today. A disabled flag is off for everyone.
The new behaviour has tests in test/. Keep each change focused on what that message asks for.
turns: Next, add setTargets(store, name, { allow, deny }), each a list of user ids. A user on the allow list is on whatever the percent, and a user on the deny list is off whatever the percent. If a user is on both lists, deny wins. A disabled flag is still off for everyone, whatever its lists say.

Next, add setPrerequisites(store, name, names). A flag is on for a user only if every flag it lists is also on for that user, through any chain of prerequisites. A name that is not a defined flag, or a list that would make a flag depend on itself through any chain, has code invalid and changes nothing.

Product has looked at the targeting again. One rule changes: when a user is on both the allow list and the deny list, allow now wins. Change the code and the tests to match, and keep everything else as it is.
brief: Add gradual rollout to the feature flags over the messages that follow: percentages, targeting lists and prerequisites, keeping the decisions in the first message binding throughout. Follow the conventions already in the code and the README, and change only what the work needs.
